messages:
Evelyn: Quick RFC follow-up — we need clear runtime semantics for Hosted / Dedicated / Private routing + fallbacks. Primary goals: keep a low-latency fast-path for Hosted, predictable throughput for Dedicated, and strong isolation for Private. Ideas?

Jasper: Propose a policy hierarchy: prefer target by hosting policy, allow fallback to Dedicated only if tenant explicitly opts in at onboarding. Private should never fall back out unless explicit emergency opt-in with legal signoff. :+1:

Anas: I get the need for isolation but totally blocking private->dedicated removes any surge protection. Suggest private->dedicated only for read-only embeddings or degraded model modes, with mandatory audit logs and encrypted-in-flight guarantees. :thinking_face:

Kai: Operationally we need a token exchange pattern if cross-domain fallback is allowed. Private uses mTLS + customer KMS; the control plane must mint short-lived tokens and strip customer secrets. @Evelyn this impacts onboarding flow.

Marco: From an SLO perspective, when we do cross-env fallback we should add a QoS signal and degrade gracefully (e.g., fall back to a smaller model or embeddings-only path) rather than full model swap. Also attach `fallback_reason` to traces.

Evelyn: Agreed. Also need a config translation shim that can map runtime features between environments. Example mapping snippet:
```
# routing-policy example
policy: 
  prefer: hosted
  fallbacks:
    - dedicated: { allowed: true, max_latency_ms: 300 }
    - private: { allowed: false }
```
The shim must validate that options like `kv_cache: enabled` actually map to runtime-supported flags for the target environment.

Jasper: Add to that: maintain a compatibility matrix keyed by model-version + quantization + runtime-capabilities. Fallback only allowed if compatibility matrix returns `ok`. Telemetry should include matrix-match-id.

Deploy-bot: deploy-bot: I can emit a `fallback_event` webhook to #incidents and #ops when a cross-host fallback happens. Suggest CI gate: run policy-mismatch tests on every infra change.

Anas: Security note — require customer-level consent toggles during onboarding for any cross-host fallback; default deny even for hosted->dedicated. Keep an audit trail and allow customers to opt-in per-call via metadata.

Kai: Edgecase: tenant-localized model weights (e.g., customer proprietary fine-tune or private data residency) cannot be moved; fallback must fail with 412 + human-readable reason.

Marco: Next steps: draft a compact decision matrix (who owns what, allowed fallbacks, telemetry fields, audit requirements). I'll own the telemetry piece; will add fields: `fallback_type`, `fallback_source`, `match_matrix_id`, `degraded_model_id`.

Evelyn: I'll draft the RFC and a small PoC config translator. Owners: @Jasper (policy), @Kai (security/token exchange), @Marco (telemetry), @Anas (ops/fallback procedures). Target: first pass by EOW. :rocket:

Jasper: :+1:

Evelyn: Linking a quick spreadsheet for decisions: https://go/infra/fallback-matrix (internal doc)

Anas: If anyone wants a short follow-up sync, ping me — happy to coordinate gate criteria and emergency rollback playbook.

Kai: Noted. I'll enumerate token flows and failure modes in the RFC.

Deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created issue INF-1423 to track RFC and CI gates.
